To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
optineurin is a binding partner of myosin Vl, and that myosin V1, optineurine, and Rab8 are required for exocytic trafficking from the TGN.
myosin VI binds to Rab8 via its cargo-binding domain and that Rab8 is essential for the function of myo VI in the exocytic trafficking pathway.
myosin VI binds to Rab8 and its effector optineurin and that myosin and optineurin are involved in the regulation of exocytic membrane transport.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification, characterization, and functional analysis of the molecular machinery involved in polarized membrane trafficking.
the analysis of the interactions and functions of optineurin and myosin VI in intracellular membrane transport pathways and the identification of the underlying molecular mechanisms.
the analysis of protein-protein interactions between optineurin and Rab8 and between optineur and myosin VI in the secretory pathways.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
myosin VI is an important component of the secretory pathway that regulates the transport of vesicles from the TGN toward the plasma membrane.
myosin VI functions in polarized membrane trafficking and that optineurin is a binding partner of Rab8 and of myosin V.
myosin VI interacts with optineurin and Rab8 and is involved in exocytosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Rab8 is a master regulator of the exocytic membrane-trafficking pathway and that optineurin and myosin VI are important effectors of Rab8 that function in the exocytic trafficking pathway.

myosin VI is a novel component of a Rab8-dependent exocytic membrane transport pathway from the TGN and the recycling compartment to the cell surface and that it interacts with Rab8 and optineurin to mediate its function.
Rab8 and its effector optineurin are involved in the exocytic trafficking of proteins to the cell surface via a myosin VI-dependent process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Rab8, optineurine and myosin VI are important for polarized trafficking of the TGN-derived vesicles and that myosin VI is a major regulator of Rab8 activity.
myosin VI is a key regulator of polarized trafficking pathways from the Golgi complex to the cell surface.
the Rab8-optineurine-myosin VI complex is important for exocytic membrane traffic in polarized cells.
